report:
Based on my research, here's my assessment:

## Report: Does Opening a Bedroom Window/Door Improve Sleep?

**The evidence is mixed, and the claim is only partially supported — the mechanism is more nuanced than "open window = better sleep."**

**What supports it:** The core mechanism is CO2/ventilation, not the window itself. Studies from DTU (Technical University of Denmark) found that opening a window or door lowers bedroom CO2 concentrations (from ~1,800+ ppm to ~750-1,000 ppm), and lower CO2 correlates with better next-day cognitive performance and perceived sleep quality ([DTU/ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0360132322008605); [dtu.dk](https://www.dtu.dk/english/newsarchive/2023/05/ventilate-your-bedroom-at-night-you-perform-better-the-next-day)). A controlled Chinese CO2-chamber study similarly found sleep quality declined as bedroom CO2 rose across simulated occupancy levels ([MDPI](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-5309/13/11/2768)).

**Important caveats:** 
1. Opening a door (rather than window) may improve air quality less effectively and not meaningfully boost sleep, per one field study.
2. A Shanghai summer study found air quality improved with windows open, but actual sleep *worsened* — likely due to heat and noise offsetting the ventilation benefit ([Sleep Foundation](https://www.sleepfoundation.org/sleep-news/open-window-may-be-better-for-sleep-but-we-keep-it-closed)).
3. If outdoor air is cold, noisy, humid, or polluted, opening a window can *reduce* sleep quality despite better CO2 levels ([AOL/lifestyle piece](https://www.aol.com/lifestyle/open-bedroom-window-winter-better-160000273.html)).
4. A DTU review notes overall evidence linking bedroom ventilation to sleep quality remains "limited."

**Conclusion:** The claim is directionally true under good conditions (mild climate, quiet, safe outdoor air) — ventilation lowering CO2 modestly helps sleep and next-day cognition. But it's not universally true; outdoor temperature, noise, and pollution can negate or reverse the benefit.
